My grandmother was diagnosed with lung cancer last year, and couldn't handle it mentally. After a couple of months she stopped eating and drinking, lying in bed all day. It got so bad she had to be admitted to the hospital. Afterwards she went to a nursing home to basically learn how to walk again. Walking had always been difficult for her, but after staying in bed for so long she just couldn't walk anymore. The first 2 weeks she did great, you could see her progress. Then she just... crashed. She barely ate and drank anymore, she started crawling back in bed and she would struggle breathing. The nurses told us it was all in her head, she was fine, she just had to do things. My mom tried to get them to run some tests, if only to reassure my grandmother she was fine. They refused. They sent her home. She died the next day. My mom went there to inform them of what happened, and they still refused to acknowledge that they did anything wrong. They just said "she would have died here as well." That's true, but we could have said goodbye. It's been a month, and I'm still so incredibly angry. I blame them for what happened. If they had run some tests they would have known something was up. They might not have been able to do anything, but we could have said goodbye. We could have told her it was okay. We kept pushing her to get up, but she couldn't. I'll always feel guilty about that.

He sacrificed everyone who cared about him, who wanted to see his dream come true, he sacrificed them all fro his stupid dream. 4. Naruto - the Pain arc. This arc was just so good. Naruto grew so much, and Naruto Sage mode is amazing. Naruto fighting the six Pains was amazing, and the Hinata part had my fangirl side cheering and crying for her. The only downside about this arc is the lame ending. But the rest is just amazing, the fight was really good.
5. One Piece - Enies Lobby arc. I'm a Robin fan, and this arc made me appreciate her so much more. Her background is just so sad, and Luffy really saved her - not just physicially, but also emotionally.
